## Coding Agent: "What is assigned to me?"
When a developer asks what they should work on: read `.s7/shared/assigned-stories.json`, match their name against `assigned_to`, then open `.s7/stories/<story>/` for that story — `story.md` for context, `acceptance-criteria.md` for the checklist, and `.s7/tasks/<task>/` for the executable task packs. Summarise the story and its acceptance criteria before implementing, plan it function by function under Build Discipline below, and implement only within Allowed Components under the Engineering Rules. If no story carries their name, say so — never guess an assignment.

## Git Workflow
All branch, commit and push rules live in `.s7/shared/git-workflow.md`. The developer owns every commit and push, and edits every plan before it is built; act on exactly five phrases:
- "start working on <story-id>" — branch, list the criteria in build order, lay the red baseline, ask the blocking questions. **Plan nothing and write no code.**
- "plan the next criterion" — write the code plan for *one* criterion into the story note and stop, so the developer can change it.
- "build the plan" — re-read that section as the developer left it, build exactly that until its test and the full suite are green, then hand them a way to see it working and stop.
- "commit the changes" — commit what was reviewed: red baseline first, implementation second, story id in every message.
- "development completed: please push the code" — run that file's push checklist in order and refuse to push if any step fails.

## Build Discipline
A story is delivered **one acceptance criterion at a time**, and each criterion goes plan → edit → build → see it working before the next one is planned. On the plan phrase, write that **one** criterion's plan into its section of the story note (`docs/delivery/<story-id>.md`): the criterion verbatim, the S7 skeleton test that proves it, the **code plan** (every function, module, template and config key to create or change, each with why *this* criterion needs it, named against code that actually exists) and how the developer will see it working. Then stop — **that section is the contract and the developer owns it**, so they may rewrite any part of it. On the build phrase, re-read the section **as they left it** and build what it now says, never what was proposed; if an edit cannot be implemented as written, say why and stop. Work inside one criterion is continuous, so nobody is asked to approve each function. Then hand them the page, command or query that shows the criterion working, wait for what they actually observed, record it in that section, tick it and stop. Later criteria are planned when their turn comes, never in advance. A criterion nobody looked at is not done, and a whole story is never generated in one pass. See the "plan the next criterion" and "build the plan" sections of `.s7/shared/git-workflow.md`.

## Story-Owned Files
Never edit a shared file (`README.md`, `architecture.md`, the shared application config, CI workflows) on a story branch — that is how parallel stories conflict on merge. Story notes go in `docs/delivery/<story-id>.md`; feature-flag defaults live in code. See the *Story-owned files* section of `.s7/shared/git-workflow.md`.

## Code Rules
How the code itself is written is governed by `.s7/shared/code-conventions.md`, and a criterion is met only when its test passes **and** the code follows it. Read it before the first line. Its first rule outranks the rest: **open the neighbouring files and follow what this repository already does** — naming, layering, how errors travel, how tests are arranged — and where the repository disagrees with the standard, the repository wins. Then: one job per function, early returns instead of deep nesting, never swallow a failure, validate every input once at the edge, log identifiers and never contents, comments say *why*, and no dead code, no speculative abstraction, no invented library calls, no secrets. Reuse what is already here before adding anything, and a new dependency is a team decision, not a story's convenience.

## Architecture Rules
Respect the integration boundaries in `.s7/shared/architecture.md`; consume other applications only through their published interfaces. Do not introduce a new architectural pattern inside a story.

## Engineering Rules
See `.s7/shared/engineering-rules.md` — scope discipline, test-first, traceability, no self-approval.
Reference the story id (and task id where relevant) in every commit message — e.g. `US-1: add sign-in form`. The Control Centre reads progress from the repository by exactly this convention.

## Acceptance Criteria
Per story under `.s7/stories/<story>/acceptance-criteria.md`. Every criterion needs linked executable evidence.

## Testing Rules
Write the failing test first; record the red baseline; a criterion without a test is not done.

## UI Rules
Every page this team adds or changes follows `.s7/shared/ui-guidelines.md` — MapleSure tokens, page anatomy, the five states every page must render, WCAG AA, and the screenshots the pull request must carry. Start from the shared layout and stylesheet under `.s7/shared/ui/` (`layout.html`, `app.css`), never from a framework default. A page that works but ignores it is not done.

## Data Rules
Every story that touches persistence follows `.s7/shared/db-conventions.md` — one forward-only migration per story, named for it and never edited after merge; a config fragment per story, never an edit to the shared config; synthetic seed data in a dev profile only.
